extracted.intended_audience: prospective and current USPTO patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), USPTO/OED staff, and applicants for registration
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing who is a 'practitioner', what constitutes practice before the USPTO, the requirements and procedures for registration (including examinations and waivers), OED Director duties, and related procedural definitions and timelines. Focused on enrollment, discipline, and the scope of authorized services before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance means a written submission from any source received by the OED Director that presents possible grounds for discipline of a specified practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Informed consent means the agreement by a person to a proposed course of conduct after the practitioner has communicated adequate information and explanation about the material risks of and reasonably available alternatives to the proposed course of conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowingly / known / knows
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowingly, known, or knows means actual knowledge of the fact in question. A person’s knowledge may be inferred from circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law-related services
rubrics_metrics.description: Law-related services means services that might reasonably be performed in conjunction with and in substance are related to the provision of legal services, and that are not prohibited as unauthorized practice of law when provided by a non-lawyer.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED (Office of Enrollment and Discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED means the Office of Enrollment and Discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director’s representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: OED Director’s representatives means attorneys within the USPTO Office of General Counsel who act as representatives of the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office means the United States Patent and Trademark Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Partner means a member of a partnership, a shareholder in a law firm organized as a professional corporation, or a member of an association authorized to practice law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Person means an individual, a corporation, an association, a trust, a partnership, and any other organization or legal entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner (who is a practitioner)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner means: (1) An attorney or agent registered to practice before the Office in patent matters under §11.6; (2) An individual authorized under 5 U.S.C. 500(b), or otherwise as provided by §11.14(a)-(c), to practice before the Office in trademark matters or other non-patent matters; (3) An individual authorized to practice before the Office in patent matters under §11.9(a) or (b); or (4) An individual authorized to practice before the Office under §11.16(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceeding before the Office (scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceeding before the Office means an application for patent, a reissue, a reexamination, a protest, a public use matter, an inter partes patent matter, correction of a patent, correction of inventorship, an application to register a trademark, an inter partes trademark matter, an appeal, a petition, and any other matter that is pending before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable / reasonably (standard of conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonable or reasonably when used in relation to conduct by a practitioner means the conduct of a reasonably prudent and competent practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable belief / reasonably believes
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonable belief or reasonably believes when used in reference to a practitioner means that the practitioner believes the matter in question and that the circumstances are such that the belief is reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonably should know (knowledge standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonably should know when used in reference to a practitioner means that a practitioner of reasonable prudence and competence would ascertain the matter in question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration means registration to practice before the Office in patent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roster or register (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Roster or register means a list of individuals who have been registered as a patent attorney, patent agent, or design patent practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screened (conflict isolation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Screened means the isolation of a practitioner from any participation in a matter through the timely imposition of procedures within a firm that are reasonably adequate under the circumstances to protect information that the isolated practitioner is obligated to protect under these USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct or other law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious crime (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Serious crime means: (1) Any criminal offense classified as a felony under U.S., state, or foreign law, or any criminal offense punishable by death or imprisonment of more than one year; or (2) Any crime whose necessary elements include interference with the administration of justice, false swearing, misrepresentation, fraud, willful failure to file income tax returns, deceit, bribery, extortion, misappropriation, theft, or an attempt/conspiracy/solicitation to commit such a 'serious crime.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant evidence of rehabilitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant evidence of rehabilitation means satisfactory evidence that is significantly more probable than not that there will be no recurrence in the foreseeable future of the practitioner’s prior disability or addiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial (degree or extent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial when used in reference to degree or extent means a material matter of clear and weighty importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspend / suspension (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspend or suspension means a temporary debarring from practice before the Office or other jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribunal (definition and adjudicative capacity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribunal means the Office, a court, an arbitrator in a binding arbitration proceeding or a legislative body, administrative agency or other body acting in an adjudicative capacity. A body acts in an adjudicative capacity when a neutral official, after presentation of evidence or legal argument, will render a binding legal judgment directly affecting a party’s interests in a particular matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: United States (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: United States means the United States of America, and the territories and possessions of the United States of America.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Director (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO Director means the Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office, or an employee of the Office delegated authority to act for the Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office in matters arising under this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing or written (definition, includes electronic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing or written means a tangible or electronic record of a communication or representation, including handwriting, typewriting, printing, photostating, photography, audio or video recording and electronic communications. A 'signed' writing includes an electronic sound, symbol or process attached to or logically associated with a writing and executed or adopted by a person with the intent to sign the writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director appointment qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director shall appoint a Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED Director). The OED Director shall be an active member in good standing of the bar of the highest court of a State.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director duties — registration and enrollment
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall receive and act upon applications for registration, prepare and grade the registration examination, maintain the register provided for in §11.5, and perform other duties in connection with enrollment and recognition of attorneys and agents as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director duties — investigations and discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall conduct investigations into moral character and reputation of individuals seeking registration or limited recognition, deny registration or recognition of individuals failing to demonstrate possession of good moral character and reputation, conduct investigations of matters involving possible grounds for discipline, and (with consent of a panel of three Committee on Discipline members) initiate disciplinary proceedings under §11.32.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except in matters meriting summary dismissal, no disposition under §11.22(h) shall be recommended or undertaken by the OED Director until the subject has been afforded an opportunity to respond to a reasonable inquiry by the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to OED Director regarding enrollment or recognition (timing & fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition from any action or requirement of the staff of OED reporting to the OED Director shall be taken to the OED Director accompanied by payment of the fee set forth in §1.21(a)(5)(i). Any such petition not filed within sixty days from the mailing date of the action or notice from which relief is requested will be dismissed as untimely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a petition will neither stay the period for taking other action nor stay other proceedings. The petitioner may file a single request for reconsideration of a decision within thirty days; filing a request for reconsideration stays the period for seeking review of the OED Director’s decision until final decision on reconsideration is issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of OED Director’s decision to USPTO Director (limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party dissatisfied with a final decision of the OED Director regarding enrollment or recognition shall seek review upon petition to the USPTO Director accompanied by payment of the fee set forth in §1.21(a)(5)(ii). Any petition not filed within thirty days after the final decision may be dismissed as untimely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition will be decided on the basis of the record before the OED Director; USPTO Director will consider no new evidence; copies of documents already of record should not be submitted; oral hearing granted only when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension/waiver of rules (extraordinary situations)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an extraordinary situation, when justice requires, any requirement of the regulations of this Part which is not a requirement of statute may be suspended or waived by the USPTO Director or designee, sua sponte, or on petition by any party, including the OED Director or representatives, subject to such other requirements as may be imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No petition under this section shall stay a disciplinary proceeding unless ordered by the USPTO Director or a hearing officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computing time (rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any time period stated in days or longer: (a) Exclude the day of the event that triggers the period; (b) Count every day, including intermediate Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays; and (c) Include the last day of the period, but if the last day is a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, the period continues to the end of the next day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register of attorneys and agents (§11.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: A register of attorneys and agents is kept in the Office on which are entered the names of all individuals recognized as entitled to represent applicants before the Office in preparation and prosecution of patent applications. Registration entitles the individuals so registered to practice before the Office only in patent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice before the Office (general scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice before the Office includes, but is not limited to, law-related service that comprehends any matter connected with the presentation to the Office or any of its officers or employees relating to a client’s rights, privileges, duties, or responsibilities under laws/regulations administered by the Office. Such presentations include preparing documents for filing, corresponding and communicating with the Office, representing a client at interviews, hearings, and meetings, and advising a client concerning matters pending or contemplated to be presented before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing proscribes a practitioner from employing or retaining non-practitioner assistants under supervision to assist in matters pending or contemplated to be presented before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice before the Office in patent matters (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes preparing or prosecuting any patent application; consulting or giving advice to a client in contemplation of filing; drafting the specification or claims; drafting an amendment or reply to an Office communication that may require written argument to establish patentability; drafting replies to communications; drafting communications for interference, derivation, reexamination proceedings, petitions, appeals to PTAB, or other patent proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration authorizes performance of services reasonably necessary and incident to preparation and prosecution of patent applications or other proceedings involving a patent application or patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific incidental services allowed (patent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Services include considering the advisability of relying upon alternative forms of protection under State law, and drafting an assignment or causing an assignment to be executed for the patent owner in contemplation of filing or prosecution when the practitioner represents the patent owner after a patent issues, provided the practitioner merely replicates terms of a previously existing oral or written obligation of assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice in design patent matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes preparing or prosecuting a design patent application; consulting or giving advice in contemplation of filing a design patent application; drafting the specification or claim of a design patent application; drafting amendments or replies that may require written argument to establish patentability; drafting communications for interference, derivation, reexamination, petitions, appeals to PTAB, or other design patent proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patent registration authorizes performance of services reasonably necessary and incident to preparation and prosecution of design patent applications or other proceedings involving a design patent application or design patent in which the practitioner is authorized to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice in trademark matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes consulting with or giving advice to a client in contemplation of filing a trademark application; preparing or prosecuting an application for trademark registration; preparing an amendment that may require written argument to establish registrability; preparing or prosecuting documents for maintaining, correcting, amending, canceling, surrendering, or otherwise affecting a registration; conducting opposition, cancellation, or concurrent use proceedings; and conducting appeals to the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may be registered — attorneys and agents (§11.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorneys: Any U.S. citizen who is an attorney and fulfills the requirements of this part may be registered as a patent attorney. Appropriate aliens who are attorneys and lawfully reside in the U.S. and fulfill requirements may be registered provided such registration is not inconsistent with their immigration status and subject to conditions for continued registration. Agents: Any U.S. citizen who is not an attorney and fulfills the requirements may be registered as a patent agent; similar conditional registration provisions for aliens who lawfully reside in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-resident aliens and continuation of registration see cross-references to §11.9(b) and §11.7(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration for foreigners (limited reciprocal recognition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any foreigner not a resident of the U.S. who files proof satisfactory to the OED Director that he/she is registered and in good standing before the patent office of the country in which he/she resides and practices, and who possesses the qualifications stated in §11.7, may be registered as a patent agent to practice before the Office for the limited purpose of presenting and prosecuting patent applications of applicants located in such country, provided the foreign patent office allows substantially reciprocal privileges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration under this paragraph continues only while the conditions obtain; OED Director shall remove and publish the fact of removal when notified the foreign registration is no longer in good standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent practitioners (§11.6(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any U.S. citizen who is an attorney and fulfills the requirements may be registered as a design patent attorney; any U.S. citizen who is not an attorney and fulfills the requirements may be registered as a design patent agent to practice in design patent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for registration (§11.7(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: No individual will be registered unless he or she has: (1) applied in writing by completing an application for registration form supplied by the OED Director and furnishing all requested information and material; and (2) established to the satisfaction of the OED Director that he or she: (i) possesses good moral character and reputation; (ii) possesses the legal, scientific, and technical qualifications necessary to render applicants valuable service; and (iii) is competent to advise and assist patent applicants in the presentation and prosecution of their applications before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness and supporting materials (§11.7(b)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete application for registration includes: (A) an application form supplied by the OED Director with all requested information and supporting documents; (B) payment of fees required by §1.21(a)(1); (C) satisfactory proof of scientific and technical qualifications; and (D) for aliens, proof that recognition is not inconsistent with visa/entry terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration examination requirement and waivers (§11.7(b)(1)(ii) & (d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must pass the registration examination unless the taking and passing is waived as provided in paragraph (d). Unless waived, each individual seeking registration must take and pass the registration examination to enable the OED Director to determine possession of legal and competence qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Former Office employees (various categories) may be eligible for waiver upon satisfying specific service, certification, performance, and timing criteria outlined in §11.7(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination retake limits and waiting periods
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual failing the examination may reapply. For first or second failure wait 30 days before retaking; for third or fourth failure wait 90 days; an individual may not take the examination more than five times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED Director may waive the five-attempt limitation upon petition under §11.2(c) and may prescribe conditions for waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete application consequences (§11.7(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual failing to file a complete application for registration will not be admitted to the examination and will be notified of the incompleteness. Incomplete applications will be considered only when completed and received by OED within 60 days of the mailing date of the notice of incompleteness; thereafter a new complete application must be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission notice and scheduling the examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of admission shall be sent to those admitted to the registration examination specifying a period to schedule and take the examination. An individual may request an extension (fee required) before expiration; granted extensions extend by 90 days. Failure to take the examination within the specified period requires filing a new application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update duty between application signing and registration (§11.7(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual seeking registration is responsible for updating all information and answers submitted in or with the application for registration based on anything occurring between the date the application is signed and the date he/she is registered or recognized. The update must be filed within thirty days after the occasion necessitating the update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver eligibility timing for former Office employees
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for consideration for waiver, an individual formerly employed by the Office within specified categories must file a complete application for registration and pay the fee within two years of the individual’s date of separation from the Office. All others formerly employed by the Office filing more than two years after separation are required to take and pass the registration examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for waiver — former examiners and employees (§11.7(d)(1)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Waiver prerequisites include: active service in patent examining corps at separation; certificate of legal competency and negotiation authority (for some categories); ratings of at least fully successful in each quality performance element for specified prior rating periods; not under an oral/written warning at separation; or demonstration of comprehensive knowledge of patent law equivalent to passing the exam via positions of responsibility and specified accomplishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination results and post-failure inspection rights (§11.7(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification of examination results is final. Within 60 days of mailing date of a notice of failure, the individual is entitled to inspect, but not copy, the questions and answers he/she incorrectly answered under supervision; no notes may be taken. Substantive review of answers or questions may not be pursued by petition for regrade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for reciprocal recognition (fee & cross-references)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual seeking reciprocal recognition under §11.6(c), in addition to satisfying provisions of paragraphs (a) and (b) and §11.8(b), shall pay the application fee required by §1.21(a)(1)(i) upon filing an application for registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation of good moral character and reputation (§11.7(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Every applicant shall answer all questions in the application and requests for information, disclose all relevant facts/dates, and provide verified copies of documents relevant to good moral character and reputation. If OED receives information adverse to good moral character/reputation, OED shall conduct an investigation after the individual has passed the exam or after waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely answer questions or respond to OED inquiry will be deemed withdrawal of the application; no individual shall be certified until, to OED’s satisfaction, the individual demonstrates possession of good moral character and reputation.
